annotation.title_clean: Robot Lawyer in Indonesian Criminal Justice System: Problems and Challenges for Future Law Enforcement
annotation.title_en: Robot Lawyer in Indonesian Criminal Justice System: Problems and Challenges for Future Law Enforcement
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Fernando, Z.J.; Kristanto, K.; Anditya, A.W.; Hartati, S.Y.; Baskara, A.
annotation.summary_en: Normative legal study of AI-based 'robot lawyers' (software) in Indonesia's criminal justice system. It sees efficiency gains in evidence gathering, case analysis and indictment drafting, but flags ethics, data security and professional qualification issues. It urges government-industry-academia collaboration on regulation and infrastructure, plus digital literacy.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot lawyers could speed evidence gathering, case analysis and indictment drafting in Indonesian criminal justice.
Challenges include ethical concerns, data security and professional qualifications.
Calls for collaboration among government, industry and academia to draft regulations and build infrastructure.
Recommends improving digital literacy and public understanding of AI in law.
